exchanges.author: c_lisa
exchanges.body: Heads up: Dayton DC may need to push ~1,500 lines a day of overflow to you in December. Can Groveport absorb it? What would it take?

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: At October productivity (7.65 lines per labor hour), 1,500 more lines a day is about 196 labor hours a day, roughly 25 more agency FTE on top of the peak plan's 61, so about 86 agency FTE, and a 13,200-line plan becomes 14,700, near our 15,400 peak day every day. Doors and dock are the constraint: we'd need Saturday shifts and the dock 7 replacement done. Doable for December with a third Pinnacle class by 11/30 and Saturdays, at about $45,000 more agency cost a month (196 h x $29 x ~22 days). I'd want Dayton's SKU list to check slotting first.

exchanges.author: c_shawn
exchanges.body: for peak motivation: pizza Friday for any team with zero injuries reported that week? keeps people careful

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Love the idea of rewarding the team, but not tied to 'zero injuries reported': it discourages reporting, which OSHA prohibits (1904.35), and we'd lose the early warnings. Let's reward the things that prevent injuries instead: completed safety huddles, near misses reported, 5S audits passed. Pizza on me either way.

exchanges.body: One correction, Beth: the clinic put Ana on full duty with no restrictions, so it's not 'job transfer or restriction'. It's 'other recordable' (medical treatment: prescription ibuprofen 800 mg), 0 days away, 0 days restricted. Everything else looks right; please enter it and the 301 by Monday 11/9, and send it to Carmen for review.

exchanges.body: Ronan, a mechanical contractor needs 40 cases of copper fittings at the Lexington branch Saturday morning for a weekend boiler job. Can you send a Saturday truck? Buckeye quoted $650 for a Saturday LTL delivery. Gary

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Yes: I'll approve the $650 Saturday run (within my authority, and we owe you after last Friday). Jasmine will stage it Friday by 1:00 and confirm the delivery window with you. Send me the order number.

exchanges.body: Ronan, we have 22 confirmed for Monday 11/9 (2 dropped for other offers). We can do a second class of up to 10 on Monday 11/16 if you confirm by Friday. Kelly, Pinnacle

exchanges.author: worker
exchanges.body: Thanks Kelly. Confirmed 22 for Monday 11/9, 6:30 a.m. orientation (safety, PPE, WMS scanners). For the second class on 11/16, please pencil in 9; I'll confirm by Friday once I have approval.

exchanges.author: worker

exchanges.body: Lisa, Groveport October: On-time 98.3% (24,712 of 25,130; target 98.0, met). Accuracy 99.78% (252,890 of 253,460 lines; target 99.8, just missed; root cause analysis for Thursday). Labor cost per line $2.99 vs target $2.95 (Sept $2.94): overtime 3,120 hours (Sept 2,410) and agency 5,260 hours. Budget: $881,082 vs $861,500, +$19,582 (+2.3%): OT premium +$8,136, agency +$14,540, packaging +$3,420, utilities +$1,260; offset by straight wages -$6,084 and repairs -$1,690. Safety: a 7th recordable (10/30 wrist sprain, prescription medication), YTD TRIR 2.98 (2.55 before); one forklift near miss, operator retrained. Peak plan attached: 1,725 hours a day needed; with Pinnacle's 22 we're about 9 agency FTE short; I recommend a second class of 9 on 11/16 ($29/hour), which needs your approval. Ronan

versions.author: worker
versions.content:
# CER: Groveport dock 7 hydraulic leveler replacement

Amount: $18,500 (Rite-Hite quote, 5 days install). Approver: Regional VP (FIN-104, up to $50,000).
Why: the leveler is 19 years old; the cylinder failed 11/3. A $6,800 repair (approved under site authority, done this week) restores it for 2-3 years, but further failures would take a door out during peak.
Timing: install in January (after peak), when 11 doors are enough.
Alternative: run to failure on the repair; risk losing 1 of 12 doors at a peak day (2,013 labor hours, ~15,400 lines).
Recommendation: approve for January.
